name: the Giardino Inglese
title: Ancient Trees in Caserta's English Garden: 7 to Find
meta_description: An English garden built for a Bourbon queen in 1786, planted with species nobody in Italy had grown before. Seven remarkable trees and where each stands.
intro: Maria Carolina of Austria wanted an English garden and got one of the first in Italy, which is why the trees here are strange. She commissioned it in 1786 at the top of the Reggia's enormous formal park, and the English gardener John Andrew Graefer filled it with species the country had barely seen: a camphor tree from Japan, a cork oak, a Douglas fir from the American northwest, a sweet osmanthus. Seven of them are on the register today. The oldest is a yew by the Bath of Venus that was carried in fully grown, which makes it older than the garden it stands in.
